Leo Tolstoy, Anna Karenina, translated by Constance Garnett.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/leo-tolstoy/anna-karenina/constance-garnett

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Leo Tolstoy, the author, died 1910 (Wikidata Q7243, P570 = 1910-11-07, 1910-11-10 and 1910-11-20).
- Constance Garnett, the translator, died 1946 (Wikidata Q2495818, P570 = 1946-12-17).

First publication of the text used: 1901 for the English translation (the Russian original was published in 1878). SE colophon: 'Anna Karenina was published in 1878 by Leo Tolstoy. It was translated from Russian in 1901 by Constance Garnett.'

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1901, before 1931, and the edition's rights statement (quoted below) places it in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin of the English text (not stated in the facts; the possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa): each has a copyright term of life plus 70 years or less. The last person to die (Garnett, 1946) makes the translation public domain in each of them no later than 1 January 2017. Country of origin of the Russian original (1878; not stated in the facts; the author's country is Russia): for Tolstoy, who died in 1910, a term of life plus 70 years ends on 31 December 1980, so the original is in the public domain from 1 January 1981. No person named above worked or fought in World War II, so the Russian wartime extension does not apply.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: Anna Karenina was published in 1878 by Leo Tolstoy. It was translated from Russian in 1901 by Constance Garnett.
- Wikidata Q7243 (Leo Tolstoy), P570 = 1910-11-07, 1910-11-10 and 1910-11-20.
- Wikidata Q2495818 (Constance Garnett), P570 = 1946-12-17.
